taxonomy.note: Accepted in the current Kew/POWO Tradescantia backbone; learner retained at species rank.

evidence: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Commelinaceae index includes Tradescantia humilis.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed local treatment of Tradescantia humilis.
Bell — Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas explicitly reports Bell County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: PASS uses explicit county-level flora/herbarium or supporting occurrence evidence; no broad ecoregion statement is converted into an unnamed county.

morphology.look_here_first: Start at the base of the plant. Texas spiderwort is low, many-stemmed and bushy at ground level, with clearly hairy vegetative shoots; toward the inflorescence the hairs become strongly glandular. That compact, fuzzy architecture separates it quickly from the taller giant and prairie spiderworts.
diagnostic_traits: compact ascending/spreading shoots, under 20 cm in the Williamson treatment
leaf blades pilose with hairs reaching several millimeters
inflorescence and pedicels conspicuously stalked-glandular hairy
terminal condensed cyme, usually 1–2 flowers open per day

confusers.separator: T. gigantea is much taller and more robust, usually one-stemmed at the base with lower stems nearly glabrous.

T. occidentalis is taller and narrower-leaved; its stem is densely long-stalked glandular-hairy but the leaf blades are largely glabrous above, rather than the overall hairy compact habit of T. humilis.

installation_guardrail: Strict PASS complete; install under standing blanket approval.
